abstract: Expansion of the primate cerebral cortex is associated with increased proliferation and diversification of neural progenitors, particularly outer radial glia (oRG), but the evolutionary developmental changes underlying these features remain unclear. Here, we integrate time-resolved, paired single-nucleus transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility profiles from human, macaque and mouse fetal cortex to compare their radial glial developmental programs. Developmental alignment within a conserved corticogenic framework identified two human-enriched programs associated with oRG features and progenitor maintenance. We identified RHOJ, which encodes a conserved small GTPase, as an oRG-enriched gene with elevated expression in human cortex. Ectopic RHOJ expression in mouse fetal cortex increased the proportions of neural progenitors and cells with oRG-like morphology, and altered the relative abundance of SATB2+ and TBR1+ neuronal populations. An intronic RHOJ enhancer showed greater reporter activity for the human sequence than for orthologous non-human primate sequences, partly attributable to a human-specific substitution within a predicted AP-1 binding motif. In human cortical organoids, deletion of this enhancer reduced RHOJ expression, impaired organoid growth and altered progenitor and neuronal populations. These findings link human-enriched developmental programs to evolutionary modification of progenitor properties, supporting altered deployment of conserved genes as a potential contributor to cortical progenitor diversification.
